title: A Simpler, Faster Way to Get Around Silq
summary: Navigation is reorganized around how you work. Projects, shipments, and inspections stay up top, related pages sit in groups, and New RFQ is on every page.
body:
Silq’s navigation has been redesigned so you can reach projects, shipments, quotes, and invoices in fewer clicks. The pages you already use are still there. Related pages now sit together, and you can decide how much of the menu stays open.

## Everything you use, organized around how you work

Projects, Shipments, and Inspections stay at the top. The rest of the menu is grouped into Quoting, Insights, My business, Tasks, and Finance.

![Grouped navigation](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/68fc03f82c0ff59fbbd1c51a/6ae18522f4bff598a316bd81_Frame%20812749%20%284%29.png)

Expand a group when you need those pages, and collapse it when you want a shorter menu. Silq remembers that setup in the browser you are using.

## Request a quote from wherever you are

New RFQ sits at the top right of every page. You can start a quote request from a project, a shipment, or an invoice, and closing the form returns you to the page you were on. Notifications, feedback, and your account sit in that same bar.

![Top bar with New RFQ](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/68fc03f82c0ff59fbbd1c51a/6ae1850c9a62378235831ea3_Top%20Navigation%20%281%29.png)

## Get back to recent work, or make room for it

A Most Visited strip along the bottom brings back the projects and shipments you open most often. On Projects it shows projects, on Shipments it shows shipments, and elsewhere it shows both. Hover a shipment for a short preview of its route before you open it. The list is yours alone.

If you are working on a map or a long list, collapse the menu into a slim row of icons. Hover an icon to see its pages.

![Collapsed navigation](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/68fc03f82c0ff59fbbd1c51a/6ae18f5ef82b53e75b5485df_Navigation%20Collapsed%20%282%29.png)

## Where things moved

- Quotes and Bookings are under Quoting.
- Reports and Analytics are under Insights.
- Documents and Network are under My business.
- Invoices are under Finance.
- Request quote is the green New RFQ button at the top right.
- Notifications and Feedback are in the top bar, with your account on your picture or initials.

> **Note:** Bookmarks and shared links keep working. Each page still uses the same web address.

Nothing was removed. Folded groups and a collapsed menu stay as you left them in this browser. A new computer or browser starts with the menu fully open.

title: Bridging The Gap Between Technology and Human Insights in Supply Chains
summary: Dashboards and automation still need people who can read the data, and Silq pairs on-site inspections with the platform so the two work as one.
body:
Technology can speed a supply chain up. It still depends on people who can read what it produces and decide what to do next. The gap shows up in a few familiar places.

## Where the gap shows up

- Teams struggle to interpret what a system is telling them when the data is not standardized or people have not been trained on it.
- Automation can free time for harder work, and it can also let problem-solving skills fade if nobody practices them.
- Data that lives in separate systems forces people to pass updates around by hand.
- A model only does what it is given. Bad inputs still produce bad outcomes.

## What closes it

Put the data in one place so people are not reconstructing a shipment from separate files. Be explicit about what the software does and what a person still decides. Train people on the tool, and keep a habit of using its data in the daily conversation rather than around it. The tool has to be simple enough that a team will actually use it.

## How Silq uses both

Silq sends people to the factory for on-site inspections, covering the work a screen cannot do: manufacturing follow-up, a shipping plan, and quality checks that cut returns. The platform then carries the rest of the chain, so the inspection and the shipment live together instead of in two systems.

> **Note:** Technology does not replace the judgment on the floor. It gives that judgment one place to land.

title: How Silq’s New Freight RFQ Form is Transforming Shipping for High-End Goods
summary: The quote request can start from an earlier RFQ, fill common fields for you, and add an inspection or other service without beginning again.
body:
Building a freight quote request used to mean retyping the lane, the cargo, and the extras every time. The RFQ form now keeps that work and lets you shape the request around the shipment in front of you.

## What the form does

- Reuse an earlier RFQ as a template, and start from the requests you send most often.
- Fill freight mode from your last accepted RFQ, and suggest ports, lanes, and carriers you already use.
- Add an inspection, warehousing, consolidation, or special handling without starting the request over.
- Switch weight between kilograms and pounds, attach an MSDS or other compliance file, and note how the cargo is palletized.
- Older RFQs still open. New fields fill in where the earlier request already had the information.

![The freight RFQ form](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/68fc03f82c0ff59fbbd1c51a/690afffb66e510142c7d6ff3_New%20Freight%20RFQ%20Form.webp)

> **Tip:** For a repeat route, start from the RFQ that already matches that lane and change only what is different.

Past requests stay available, so you can look back at how a lane was quoted before you send the next one. An inspection or another service can be added on the same request.

title: Elevate Your Shipment Visibility with Silq’s New Dashboards
summary: Shipments and Projects each have a dashboard with list, map, and hybrid views, a node you can open for status, and comments on the shipment.
body:
Shipments and projects now share a dashboard, so the file is not split across separate tools. You can watch a shipment from the factory through delivery and catch a delay before it becomes a missed delivery.

## Pick the view that matches the question

- Hybrid puts the list beside the map.
- List is the breakdown of every project and shipment.
- Map shows where the cargo is.

![Shipments dashboard](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/68fc03f82c0ff59fbbd1c51a/690b44b3020f96f58bc4cf27_Shipments%20Dashboard_Double%20click%20view.jpg)

## Open a shipment from the map

Each shipment node opens the status, the location, and the timeline for that move. Use it when a box is nearing a busy port or coming up on delivery and you need the date, not just the pin.

## Comments stay on the shipment

Add a comment on the dashboard and the people on that file see it there, instead of in a separate thread. Alerts surface a delay early enough to reroute, move a date, or call a partner while the shipment is still moving.

> **Note:** The same dashboard covers the path from production to delivery, so the team, the supplier, and the forwarder are looking at one file.

title: A concise yet comprehensive Projects Dashboard
summary: Each project card shows the work in progress, the due date, and stage dates on hover, and a red mark when a milestone is behind plan.
body:
The Projects dashboard is a single view of the work on your account: status, what is in progress, and whether a stage is slipping.

## On each card

- The project name, picture, Silq ID, current work, due date, and timeline.
- The stage that is underway, including what is done and what is still open.
- Hover a stage for the planned, estimated, and actual dates, without opening the project.
- Filter to a phase, such as production or shipping.
- A red mark on a milestone that is behind the plan.

![Projects dashboard](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/68fc03f82c0ff59fbbd1c51a/690b35820fcba8903cd66280_Projects%20dashboard.png)

> **Tip:** Use the phase filter when you only need the projects in production or the ones already shipping.

Open Projects after you sign in. The hover dates are there so a status check does not require the detail page.

title: Transparent quoting with My Rates
summary: My Rates shows your lane rates by mode, including shared container, with the charge breakdown, an estimated transit time, and a rate you can lock for a month.
body:
My Rates opens the rates already set up for your lanes, so a quote does not start from a blank request. You can compare modes, including Silq’s shared container load, and see how the port-to-port price is built.

## What you can do

- See your rates for each mode on a lane.
- Compare them and pick the one that costs less for that shipment.
- Lock a rate for up to a month.
- Read the estimated transit time next to the mode.
- Open the rate by charge, not only as a single number.
- Price a shared container when a full container is more space than you need.

![My Rates](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/68fc03f82c0ff59fbbd1c51a/690c7eb33abef2b73705ea75_My%20Rates.png)

## How to lock a rate

1. Sign in and open My Rates.
2. Adjust the shipment details.
3. Compare the modes.
4. Submit the rate request to lock it for a month.

> **Note:** My Rates is port to port for now. Port to door is planned as a follow-up.

If the page is not on your account, your account manager can turn it on.

title: Introducing Our New Side Navigation Panel
summary: The header and the menu became one side panel, which frees a row on every page and shows notification counts next to the pages they belong to.
body:
The side panel replaced the separate header and menu. Pages sit in one list, and the content area gains the row the header used to take.

## What changed

- The header and the navigation are one panel, so you are not looking in two places for the same page.
- Removing the header gives every page another row of content.
- Counts and notification marks sit on the panel, next to the area they refer to.

![Side navigation](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/68fc03f82c0ff59fbbd1c51a/6903f019785c21f1e6d30dcd_64c2f4413656101dd6fc2c21_IyVhx7mcfRICGapYJ08QddEztOGxCiLrr7ZzeTMfn9fhinurBqqZYiVIwu95Yr9sjqn7gxNXUBUKmI-LcqwYvVqaLpRh3fmOxYGkk9Ojgqyz1zNOAI9jJ_5HUkrOUB7lnuEC1ZVnvAh0r0i8Wm8InfE.png)

> **Note:** This is the earlier navigation update. The October 2026 redesign groups those same pages and adds New RFQ to the top bar.
